findings.title: Exhausted recovery codes in user storage are not removed by removeStoredCredentialById
findings.body: When `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(authenticatedUser)` returns a credential from a federated `UserStorageProvider` (via `getFederatedCredentialsStream()`) and `recoveryCodeCredentialModel.allCodesUsed()` is true, calling `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(...)` only invokes `CredentialProvider.deleteCredential(...)` on local credential providers and has no effect on a `UserStorageProvider`. `UserStorageProvider` implementations of `CredentialInputUpdater` do not support deletion by ID and instead remove credentials via `disableCredentialType(RealmModel, UserModel, String)` (the fallback used by `AccountCredentialResource` when `removeStoredCredentialById` returns `false`). As a result, exhausted recovery code credentials stored in external user storage remain present after all codes have been used.

findings.title: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage does not consume used recovery codes or preserve credential ID
findings.body: In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage`, `isValid` validates recovery codes with `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))` without checking that the input matches the next expected code and without removing the used code from `myUser.recoveryCodes`. Consequently, `getCredentials` (lines 235-242) always reconstructs a `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` with all codes unused, so the login form always prompts for code #1 and allows the same code to be reused indefinitely. Additionally, `getCredentials` does not guard against `myUser == null` (unlike `isConfiguredFor`, `isValid`, and `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream`), does not copy `myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()` (set on line 195) onto the returned `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel`, and `disableCredentialType` / `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` were not updated to support `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE`.
